# ENG1 resource completion candidate handoff

Private candidate only; no canonical source, `recovery.json`, asset, or Git state was changed. The native instruction spans are pinned to `assets/pc/HERCULES/ENG1.DLL` SHA-256 `01b78ae814892007bb6031b2470f10e09bdd912fdb8d30de9f4cfea7c638f757`.

`candidates/eng1_resource_completion/resource_completion.c` supplies five behavioral candidates: compaction/rebind helper `0x1f6a0`, row loader `0x1f9e0`, async success callback `0x1fb90`, async failure callback `0x1fc60`, and root postprocessor `0x1fc90`. `resource_completion_data.c` defines only the observed writable byte at `0x70c50`; it makes no claim about adjacent storage. The source uses the existing `EngineInterface`, `ResourceCallbackContext`, descriptor-row, resource-row and allocation-slot views.

The caller evidence is direct: `0x1f750` calls `0x1fc90` at `0x1f835`, passing the loaded file length (unused by the callee); `0x1f870` calls `0x1f9e0` at `0x1f962`, `0x1f9af` and `0x1f9bf`; `0x1f9e0` calls `0x1f6a0(0)` at `0x1fa77`. Its async path stores the success/failure callbacks into the live context at `+0xb0` and `+0xb4`; the sync path invokes the success callback directly.

`0x1f9e0` rejects only `row >= (signed char)0x70ecf`; it has no lower-bound check. It reads an unsigned WORD at row record `+0`, and sign-extends the WORD at `+2`. Allocation size follows the native 32-bit expression `(((u32)(s32)size << 11) & 0xfffff800) + 0x1000`. Existing row pointers are released with `0x2c2d0`; allocation is through the existing `engine_pool_allocate(&slot, size, 0x20)` provider, preserving the pointer-cell ownership. If that pointer remains null, the source calls `0x1f6a0(0)` once and retries once. It then stores the requested row byte at `0x70c50`.

For mode zero, native order is `0x2c400(prefix,suffix)`, `0x2c4f0(row_word_000)`, reload active category and row slot, `0x2c480(slot,load_mode)`, `0x2c280()`, then `0x1fb90()`. For nonzero mode, the loader registers both callbacks, reloads active category and slot, reloads the interface context for the signed level byte, then calls the existing `engine_file_load_async(prefix,suffix,sector_offset,slot,(u32)(s32)size)` provider. `0x1f6a0` uses the existing pool-compaction provider, repeating only for a nonzero input; after compaction it reuses the existing `resource_rebuild_blob` (`0x20670`) and `resource_rebuild_group_rows` (`0x208f0`) providers when the root owner is nonnull.

`0x1fb90` uses the signed row word at `+0x10` to subtract a `<<6` displacement from the camera and a `<<22` displacement from the existing frame actor cell. In a transition it selects the transition category, rereads that byte after the first selector call, selects again, resets the transition byte to `0xff`, releases nonnull pointers in the observed 4-by-8 slot walk, restores the queued row, and rebuilds row pointers. `0x1fc60` forwards the current category/queued-row slot to the existing free provider without a null check or slot clear. Neither callback implies that 32 is the original total slot capacity.

`0x1fc90` ignores its input. It retains the first root pointer for two calls to the existing `dispatch_engine_2c7f0` provider, using packed relative DWORDs at `root+0x14` and `root+0x18`. The exact four-WORD stack descriptors are `[0,0,0x300,0x200]` and `[0x300,0x100,0x100,0x100]`; semantic field names are unknown. The return is `old_field_address + DWORD[old_root+0x20] - freshly reloaded root_owner`, preserving the native post-callback reload at `0x1fd00`.

The source leaves three wrapper bodies explicit as RVA-named external dependencies because the source-owned thunks are still missing: `0x2c400` forwards two pointer arguments through copied-interface offset `0x80` (slot 32; host callback RVA `0x3c50`); `0x2c4f0` forwards one DWORD through offset `0xc0` (slot 48; host callback RVA `0x3ce0`); `0x2c480` forwards `(pointer,DWORD)` through offset `0x9c` (slot 39; host callback RVA `0x3d00`). Their callback names and semantics are left open. The source reuses the existing providers at `calibration/engine_file_bridge.c`, `calibration/frame_lifecycle_bridges.c`, `calibration/resource_rebind.c`, and `src/eng1/behavioral/host_wrappers.c`; it does not duplicate those methods.
